product-research.name: Schwartz 5 Stages of Market Sophistication
product-research.one_line: Five-stage scale of how many similar products/claims a market has already seen: (1) First-in-market plain claim, (2) Enlarge/outbid the claim, (3) New Mechanism in headline, (4) Elaborate the mechanism, (5) Exhausted market equals identification. Markets retrace; sub-niches restart at Stage 1.
product-research.use_in_skill: 01 product-research (niche viability + copy approach) and 03 competitor-analysis
product-research.best_query: Schwartz market sophistication 5 stages mechanism claims

product-research.name: Schwartz 5 Levels of Product-Market Awareness
product-research.one_line: Scale of prospect knowledge: Unaware to Problem-Aware to Solution-Aware to Product-Aware to Most-Aware; each dictates a different headline; Product/Most-Aware refer to the CATEGORY not your brand.
product-research.use_in_skill: 01 product-research (awareness as a difficulty factor) and 02 market-research
product-research.best_query: Schwartz five stages of awareness Unaware Problem Solution Product Most aware

product-research.name: AI Deep-Research Market Awareness Prompt (TAM + distribution)
product-research.one_line: Prompt run in Gemini/GPT/Perplexity/Kimi returning TAM estimate, percent of TAM in each awareness stage, and a final dominant-stage selection to drive the funnel decision.
product-research.best_query: deep research prompt market awareness TAM percentage distribution final selection

product-research.name: Schwartz Mass Desire Theory + 3-Stage Channeling
product-research.one_line: Advertising channels existing desire, never creates it. Choose the most powerful desire by Urgency x Staying Power x Scope, acknowledge it in one headline, show product performances satisfying it.
product-research.use_in_skill: 01 product-research (does the product hit a strong mass desire) and 02 market-research
product-research.best_query: Schwartz mass desire theory channeling urgency staying power scope

product-research.name: Permanent Forces vs Forces of Change
product-research.one_line: Two roots of desire: Permanent Forces (mass instincts + mass technological problems) and Forces of Change (style/trends + mass education shifting HOW desires get satisfied). Channel the permanent, time the change.
product-research.best_query: permanent forces forces of change mass instincts technological problems style trends

product-research.name: Six Mass Instincts (operational eComm taxonomy)
product-research.source: Operational taxonomy derived from Schwartz mass desire
product-research.one_line: 6-bucket eComm version: Health, Sex, Status, Belonging, Control, Comfort, paired with 6 Mass Technological Problems (Complexity, Overwhelm, Fragility, Maintenance, Incompatibility, Obsolescence).
product-research.best_query: six mass instincts health sex status belonging control comfort technological problems

product-research.name: Cashvertising Life-Force 8 (LF8)
product-research.one_line: Eight biologically hardwired desires: survival/life-extension, food/drink, freedom from fear/pain/danger, sexual companionship, comfortable living, superiority/winning, care of loved ones, social approval. Lead with LF8.
product-research.best_query: Cashvertising Life-Force 8 LF8 Whitman biological desires

product-research.name: Cashvertising 9 Learned (Secondary) Wants
product-research.one_line: Nine learned wants weaker than LF8: to be informed, curiosity, cleanliness, efficiency, convenience, dependability/quality, beauty/style, economy/profit, bargains. Layer in after LF8.
product-research.best_query: Cashvertising nine secondary learned wants convenience curiosity efficiency

product-research.name: Cashvertising Desire Formula (Tension to Desire to Action)
product-research.one_line: Mechanical conversion of desire to sale: create tension via the unfulfilled need, stoke desire via the path to fulfillment, drive action by making purchase easy and urgent.
product-research.best_query: Cashvertising desire formula tension desire action

product-research.name: Hormozi Starving Crowd / Market Selection (4 Indicators)
product-research.one_line: Select the market before the offer via four indicators: Massive Pain, Purchasing Power, Easy to Target, Growing Market. Missing one and even a Grand Slam Offer underperforms.
product-research.best_query: Hormozi starving crowd market selection four indicators massive pain purchasing power

product-research.name: Halbert Starving Crowd Principle (original source)
product-research.one_line: Hamburger-stand parable: the greatest advantage is a hungry market. A starving crowd buys mediocre products with mediocre copy; no copy genius overcomes a market that does not want what you sell.
product-research.best_query: Halbert starving crowd hamburger stand principle market first

product-research.name: Halbert Market-First Thinking / Product-Market Inversion
product-research.one_line: Identify a hot proven market (buyers who spent money recently and repeatedly) BEFORE selecting a product, via Audience Insights/Trends/Amazon Best Sellers/subreddits/ad libraries; evaluate with RFU; only then brainstorm products.
product-research.best_query: Halbert market-first thinking product-market inversion starving crowd

product-research.name: Halbert RFU Framework (Recency, Frequency, Unit of Sale)
product-research.one_line: Grade a buyer market by Recency (recent buyers more responsive), Frequency (how often), Unit of Sale (spend). High on all three equals a hot monetizable market.
product-research.best_query: Halbert RFU recency frequency unit of sale buyer evaluation

product-research.name: Bird Relative Importance of Variables (List over Creative)
product-research.source: Drayton Bird, Commonsense Direct and Digital Marketing
product-research.one_line: Audience/list selection has about 6x more impact on results than creative, the single most important insight in direct marketing. Market choice dominates creative quality.
product-research.best_query: Bird relative importance of variables list selection 6x more than creative

product-research.name: Hopkins Category Economics (Pork-and-Beans Insight)
product-research.one_line: Understanding what behavior/category you are replacing matters more than studying direct competitors. Frames a product against the real alternative the prospect currently uses.
product-research.best_query: Hopkins category economics pork and beans replacing behavior competitive landscape

product-research.name: Bencivenga Fuzzy Dice Principle (Sell Vertically)
product-research.one_line: Intercept prospects where they are already looking: find where ideal buyers congregate and meet them there with a targeted message, rather than broadcasting horizontally.
product-research.best_query: Bencivenga fuzzy dice principle sell vertically intercept prospects

product-research.name: Bencivenga Pre-Existing Motivation + Motivated 5% Rule
product-research.one_line: You cannot create motivation; find what people already want and show your product gets it. The motivated 5 percent need full detail; writing to the unmotivated 95 percent wastes spend.
product-research.use_in_skill: 01/02 (does a real pre-existing desire exist) and 06 copy
product-research.best_query: Bencivenga pre-existing motivation motivated 5 percent rule long copy

product-research.name: Brunson Market Depth Model (Core Market / Submarket / Niche)
product-research.one_line: Three layers: Core Market (Health/Wealth/Relationships, too broad), Submarket (e.g. weight loss, crowded), Niche (your unique mechanism times a specific sub-avatar desire). You CREATE a niche.
product-research.use_in_skill: 01 product-research niche definition; 02 avatar; 04 offer mechanism
product-research.best_query: Brunson Expert Secrets market depth core market submarket niche three levels

product-research.name: Brunson Traffic Temperature (Hot/Warm/Cold)
product-research.one_line: Translates Schwartz awareness into traffic: Hot (knows you equals Most/Product-Aware), Warm (Solution-Aware), Cold (Problem/Unaware). Never send cold traffic straight to a sales page.
product-research.use_in_skill: 01/02 (map awareness to traffic) and 10 ad-strategy / 07a page bridge
product-research.best_query: Brunson DotCom Secrets traffic temperature hot warm cold awareness mapping

product-research.name: Ries and Trout Positioning: Ladder, Rule of Seven, Law of Leadership
product-research.source: Al Ries & Jack Trout, Positioning: The Battle for Your Mind
product-research.one_line: Positioning is what you do to the prospect mind. Brands rank on category ladders (room for 3-7); first brand gets about 2x No.2 and 4x No.3. If you cannot be first, create a category you can be first in.
product-research.use_in_skill: 01 product-research (can you own a position) and 03 competitor-analysis
product-research.best_query: Ries Trout positioning mental ladder rule of seven law of leadership be first

product-research.name: Ries and Trout: Cherchez le Creneau (8 Holes in the Mind)
product-research.one_line: Eight unoccupied mental positions: size, high-price, low-price, sex, age, time-of-day, distribution, heavy-user. Warns of the Factory Creneau and Technology traps.
product-research.best_query: Ries Trout cherchez le creneau eight holes in the mind size price age

product-research.name: Ries and Trout: Positioning Strategies (First/Against/Reposition/Attribute/User)
product-research.one_line: Five ways to position: be first, against the leader (Avis), reposition the competition (Tylenol vs aspirin), own a different attribute, or position by user (Marlboro). Be different, not better.
product-research.best_query: positioning strategies being first against the leader repositioning by attribute by user

product-research.name: Technical Viability Criteria (economic gate)
product-research.one_line: Hard pre-filters: AOV after bundles above $60, minimum 3x markup on COGS+shipping (5x ideal), Google Trends flat or growing over 5 years, lightweight/low-logistics. Broken economics: discard immediately.
product-research.best_query: technical viability criteria AOV markup 3x Google Trends lightweight product filter

product-research.name: Three Factors That Determine Product Difficulty
product-research.one_line: Difficulty equals Desire Magnitude (stronger equals easier sale, higher ticket), Market Awareness stage (higher equals harder), and Market Sophistication (more saturated equals need new angle). Saturation alone is not bad, it means a big audience.
product-research.best_query: three factors determine difficulty desire magnitude market awareness sophistication

product-research.name: Two Forms of Differentiation (Mechanism vs Avatar Innovation)
product-research.one_line: If you cannot differentiate, avoid the product. (a) Mechanism Innovation, a new way to solve the problem (Shilajit gummies; True Classic renaming the fit); or (b) Avatar Innovation, a segment competitors ignore (40+ women).
product-research.best_query: two forms of differentiation mechanism innovation avatar innovation overlooked avatar

product-research.name: AI Final-Validation Ranking (4-AI Deep Search)
product-research.one_line: Screenshot 10 shortlisted product pages, send to Gemini/GPT/Perplexity/Kimi via Deep Search, rank by scale potential, low strong-brand competition, unique-mechanism ability, offer/upsell room, positive feedback, niche trend, economic viability.
product-research.best_query: final validation Gemini GPT Perplexity Kimi rank products scale potential unique mechanism

product-research.name: Schwab Win / Be / Save-Avoid + 11 Appeals
product-research.source: Victor Schwab, How to Write a Good Advertisement
product-research.one_line: Three universal drivers (Win, Be, Save/Avoid) plus 11 appeal categories (Health, Comfort, Money, Leisure, Popularity, Pride, Appearance, Business/Career, Security, Status, Compliments) mapped to interior monologue.
product-research.best_query: Schwab win be save avoid eleven appeals interior monologue

product-research.name: Collier Six Prime Motives of Human Action
product-research.source: Robert Collier, The Robert Collier Letter Book
product-research.one_line: Six purchase motives: Love, Gain, Duty, Pride, Self-indulgence, Self-preservation. One rarely compels alone; Gain easiest to use, Love most powerful but hardest.
product-research.best_query: Collier six prime motives love gain duty pride self-indulgence self-preservation

product-research.name: Market Cyclicality (2-3 year cycles, markets retrace)
product-research.source: Operational principle extending Schwartz markets retrace
product-research.one_line: Markets are cyclical (about 2-3 years); what works today can be recycled from the past, and sub-niches restart at sophistication Stage 1 while the parent sits at Stage 4-5. Swipe-file year-by-year analysis surfaces these cycles.
product-research.best_query: market cyclical 2-3 years markets retrace swipe file recycle past

product-research.name: Product Evaluation Framework: Desire × Awareness × Sophistication (+ Selection Template)

product-research.name: Filtros Kalodata refinados (versão atual)
product-research.source: Aura KB — tema 'Pesquisa de Mercado e Concorrencia' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)

product-research.name: Similarweb Revenue Estimation (visits × 1% CVR × AOV)

product-research.name: Conviction Test (o produto realmente funciona?)
product-research.source: Aura KB — tema 'Pesquisa de Mercado e Concorrencia' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)

product-research.name: Rip Method + Borrowed Time (com limpeza de metadata)
product-research.source: Aura KB — tema 'Pesquisa de Mercado e Concorrencia' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)

product-research.name: Validação de demanda sem estoque (teste com refund)
product-research.source: Aura KB — tema 'Pesquisa de Mercado e Concorrencia' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)

product-research.name: Auditoria de Produto / 8-Figure Blueprint (o produto como multiplicador)
product-research.source: Aura KB — tema 'Pesquisa de Mercado e Concorrencia' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)

product-research.name: 3 tipos de tendência de mercado (Conteúdo / Consumo / Marketing)
product-research.source: Aura KB — tema 'Pesquisa de Mercado e Concorrencia' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
product-research.one_line: Separar tendência de conteúdo, tendência de consumo e tendência de marketing como três fenômenos distintos, e usar essa distinção como critério decisivo para entrar ou não em um nicho.

product-research.name: Avatar Selection Matrix
product-research.source: Aura KB — tema 'Arquitetura de Avatar' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
product-research.one_line: Cruzar magnitude do desejo com nível de competição numa matriz para escolher qual avatar atacar, funcionando como um quick kill que descarta rápido os públicos que não valem o esforço.

market-research-voc.source: Joanna Wiebe (Copyhackers) + classic review-mining tradition

market-research-voc.name: 4-Star Review Mining (avoid 1s and 5s)
market-research-voc.source: review-mining practitioners (Copyhackers tradition)
market-research-voc.one_line: Focus on 4-star reviews because 5s and 1s are often fake or pure enthusiasm/rage; the middle holds the most honest, usable language about what drove purchase and what fell short.
market-research-voc.use_in_skill: 02 market research; 03 competitor analysis (mining competitor reviews)

market-research-voc.name: Google Review-Mining Shortcuts (site:amazon.com inurl product-reviews)
market-research-voc.source: Copyhackers / Joanna Wiebe
market-research-voc.one_line: Search operators ('tired of', 'wasn't until', 'tried') combined with site:amazon.com inurl:product-reviews + ~keyword to surface VOC snippets mapped to specific awareness stages.

market-research-voc.best_query: Amazon review mining google shortcut tired of wasn't until tried site operator

market-research-voc.name: Eugene Schwartz — 5 Stages of Awareness
market-research-voc.source: Eugene Schwartz, Breakthrough Advertising (Ch. 2)
market-research-voc.one_line: Unaware → Problem Aware → Solution Aware → Product Aware → Most Aware; measures how much the prospect knows about how your product satisfies his desire, and dictates headline, copy length and education depth.
market-research-voc.use_in_skill: 02 (determine market awareness) → drives 06 copy, 07a page, 10 ad strategy
market-research-voc.best_query: Schwartz five stages of awareness unaware problem aware solution aware product aware most aware

market-research-voc.name: Awareness Stage Headline Strategy (5 stages + 7 superiority tasks)
market-research-voc.source: Eugene Schwartz, Breakthrough Advertising (Ch. 2)
market-research-voc.one_line: Each awareness stage has a distinct headline approach (Most Aware = product+price; Stage 2 'knows product not yet wanting' = 7 superiority tasks; down to identification for unaware); a headline that works at one stage fails at another.
market-research-voc.best_query: Schwartz awareness stage headline strategy seven tasks superiority approaches

market-research-voc.name: Awareness TAM Distribution (awareness pyramid)
market-research-voc.source: Schwartz framework as applied in DR market research
market-research-voc.one_line: Most Aware ~1%, Product Aware ~10-15%, Solution Aware ~15-20%, Problem Aware 30-40%, Unaware 30-40% of TAM; 70-80% of most markets sit in problem-aware/unaware, the largest growth pool but costliest to convert.
market-research-voc.use_in_skill: 02 market research (TAM + awareness % estimate); 10 ad strategy targeting
market-research-voc.best_query: awareness levels percentage TAM distribution problem aware unaware easiest convert

market-research-voc.name: Eugene Schwartz — 5 Stages of Market Sophistication
market-research-voc.source: Eugene Schwartz, Breakthrough Advertising (Ch. 3)
market-research-voc.one_line: First-to-market → enlarge the claim → New Mechanism → mechanism elaboration → exhausted/identification; measures how many competing claims the market has heard and how skeptical it is (distinct from awareness).
market-research-voc.best_query: market sophistication five stages Schwartz mechanism claim escalation jaded market

market-research-voc.name: Market Sophistication Headline Templates (by stage)
market-research-voc.source: Eugene Schwartz, Breakthrough Advertising (Ch. 3)
market-research-voc.one_line: Stage-specific headline structures: direct claim → enlarged/extreme → mechanism-in-headline+compressed-claim → improved mechanism → pure identification; plus the 'markets retrace' insight (sub-niches restart at stage 1).
market-research-voc.best_query: market sophistication headline templates by stage markets retrace insight cigarette cycle

market-research-voc.name: Three Strategic Responses for Sophisticated Markets (New Mechanism / New Information / New Identity)
market-research-voc.source: Schwartz sophistication theory, modern eCom application
market-research-voc.one_line: In stage 3-5 markets, break resistance via New Mechanism (new HOW/tech/process), New Information (educate on hidden why), or New Identity (tribal/lifestyle belonging) — each gives new hope the product will work.
market-research-voc.best_query: New Mechanism New Information New Identity three strategic responses sophisticated markets

market-research-voc.name: Avatar-Market Sophistication Gap
market-research-voc.source: modern eCom application of Schwartz
market-research-voc.one_line: Even with a perfectly defined avatar, crystal-clear desires and a product that delivers, ads fail if the message does not break through the market's sophistication level — sophistication is not something you test, it just exists.
market-research-voc.best_query: avatar market sophistication gap ads dont work not testable

market-research-voc.name: Eugene Schwartz — Mass Desire Theory (3-Stage Channeling)
market-research-voc.source: Eugene Schwartz, Breakthrough Advertising (Ch. 1)
market-research-voc.one_line: Advertising cannot create desire, only channel pre-existing mass desire; choose the strongest applicable desire, acknowledge/reinforce it in the headline, then show how the product satisfies it (the ~$50 Amplification Effect vs $1 for fighting desire).
market-research-voc.best_query: mass desire Schwartz channeling process amplification effect cannot create desire

market-research-voc.name: Desire Power Ranking — Scope / Urgency / Staying Power
market-research-voc.source: Eugene Schwartz, Breakthrough Advertising (Ch. 1)
market-research-voc.one_line: Rate every desire your product can tap on three dimensions — Scope (how many share it), Urgency (how intensely they want relief), Staying Power (how repeatedly it renews) — and pick the strongest; scope matters most.
market-research-voc.use_in_skill: 01 product research validation; 02 market research desire ranking
market-research-voc.best_query: mass desire scope urgency staying power power ranking choose strongest

market-research-voc.name: Permanent Forces vs Forces of Change
market-research-voc.source: Eugene Schwartz, Breakthrough Advertising (Ch. 1)
market-research-voc.one_line: Desires arise from Permanent Forces (mass instincts + mass technological problems — never change) and are shifted by Forces of Change (style/trends + mass education); marketers channel the permanent and time the changing.
market-research-voc.use_in_skill: 02 market research (root of desire); 01 product research trend timing
market-research-voc.best_query: permanent forces forces of change mass instinct technological problems style trends education

market-research-voc.name: Cashvertising — Life-Force 8 (LF8)
market-research-voc.source: Drew Eric Whitman, Cashvertising

market-research-voc.source: Victor Schwab, How to Write a Good Advertisement

market-research-voc.source: Russell Brunson, Expert Secrets

market-research-voc.one_line: Hot (knows you) / Warm (knows someone who knows you) / Cold (stranger) maps to Schwartz awareness; never send cold traffic straight to a sales page — it needs a pre-frame bridge first.
market-research-voc.best_query: Brunson traffic temperature hot warm cold pre-frame bridge dotcom secrets

market-research-voc.name: Schwartz↔TTM↔Brunson Awareness Mapping Table
market-research-voc.source: synthesis of Schwartz / Whitman TTM / Brunson
market-research-voc.one_line: Cross-walk table aligning each Schwartz awareness stage with its TTM behavior stage, Brunson traffic temperature, and the correct copy approach for that combination.
market-research-voc.use_in_skill: 02 market research synthesis; 06/07a/10 copy & funnel decisions
market-research-voc.best_query: Schwartz TTM Brunson awareness mapping table copy approach by stage

market-research-voc.name: Carry-Forward Through All Awareness Stages
market-research-voc.source: awareness application to eCom (Schwartz-derived rule)
market-research-voc.one_line: Wherever you enter the conversation (e.g., Problem Aware), you MUST carry the prospect forward through every subsequent stage before asking for the sale — build the full bridge, don't just identify the stage.
market-research-voc.best_query: carry forward through all stages of awareness build complete bridge before the sale

market-research-voc.name: Jobs To Be Done — The Switch & Four Forces
market-research-voc.source: Bob Moesta & Clayton Christensen (JTBD); applied by Joanna Wiebe
market-research-voc.one_line: Customers 'hire' a product for a functional/emotional/social job; The Switch is driven by four forces — Push (problem) + Pull (attraction) vs Anxiety (of the new) + Habit (of the now) — and conquering switching friction alone can multiply conversions.
market-research-voc.use_in_skill: 02 market research (deepest layer); 06 copy objection handling
market-research-voc.best_query: Jobs to be Done switch push pull anxiety habit four forces Moesta Christensen

market-research-voc.name: JTBD Switch Interview (timeline method)
market-research-voc.source: Bob Moesta, Rewired Group; Joanna Wiebe
market-research-voc.one_line: 45-60 min interview that walks the customer back through a timeline (first thought → Event 1 → Event 2 → buying → first use) using environmental/scene-setting questions to surface the forces of change; ~7 interviews ≈ 500 survey responses of insight.
market-research-voc.use_in_skill: 02 market research (qualitative); when interviews are available
market-research-voc.best_query: JTBD switch interview timeline first thought event buying first use environmental questions

market-research-voc.name: Push & Pull Questions + The Switch (Conversion Copywriting)
market-research-voc.source: Joanna Wiebe, Copyhackers (Conversion Copywriting)
market-research-voc.one_line: Research framework: Push (what problems drive them to seek a solution) + Pull (what desires draw them to it) + the often-skipped Switch (what prevents them leaving their status quo); research best done with prospects about-to-switch and recent switchers.
market-research-voc.use_in_skill: 02 market research; 06 copy; 07a page empathy section
market-research-voc.best_query: push pull questions the switch switching costs status quo conversion copywriting research

market-research-voc.name: Core Avatars & Sub-Avatars — The Core Five Categories
market-research-voc.source: avatar-building methodology (Eugene Schwartz-influenced)
market-research-voc.one_line: Build avatars from five categories in priority order — Desire > Experience ≈ Emotion ≈ Behavior > Demographics; start the core avatar with a single (surface-level) desire and stack categories to create money-making sub-avatars; 'out-avatar them, don't out-market them.'
market-research-voc.use_in_skill: 02 market research avatar build; 08 creatives angle-per-avatar; 10 targeting
market-research-voc.best_query: core avatar sub avatar core five categories desire experience emotion behavior demographic

market-research-voc.name: Desire-First Avatar (over Demographics)
market-research-voc.source: avatar-building methodology
market-research-voc.one_line: Demographics alienate and are weak starting points (a 22yo and 45yo share the same desire); start from a shared desire because desires drive purchase behavior and create the group label — avoid combining more than one desire per avatar.
market-research-voc.best_query: desire first avatar over demographics avoid combining desires single desire core avatar

market-research-voc.name: Surface Desire vs Core Desire
market-research-voc.source: avatar-building methodology (Schwartz desire theory)
market-research-voc.one_line: Build avatars on surface-level desires ('I want better sleep') for specificity, but dig in research for the underlying core desire (the why) to guide messaging and sub-avatar creation.

competitor-positioning.name: Reeves' Unique Selling Proposition (USP) — 3-Part Test
competitor-positioning.source: Rosser Reeves, Reality in Advertising (1961)
competitor-positioning.one_line: Every USP must simultaneously pass three tests: a specific Proposition (buy this, get this benefit), Uniqueness (competition cannot or does not offer it), and Selling Power (strong enough to move the mass millions).
competitor-positioning.use_in_skill: 04 (offer — core USP), 03 (competitor analysis — testing whether a gap is ownable)
competitor-positioning.best_query: USP unique selling proposition Reeves three requirements proposition uniqueness selling power

competitor-positioning.name: Three Roads to a USP (Three Roads to Rome)
competitor-positioning.source: Rosser Reeves, Reality in Advertising
competitor-positioning.one_line: Three ways to build a USP: Road 1 find a real product difference; Road 2 improve the product to create one; Road 3 claim something true but previously unmentioned (the preemptive claim).
competitor-positioning.best_query: three roads to a USP find real difference improve product preemptive claim

competitor-positioning.name: The Preemptive Claim (Schlitz / Live Steam)
competitor-positioning.source: Claude Hopkins, Scientific Advertising (original); Reeves Road 3
competitor-positioning.one_line: In categories where products are functionally identical, the first brand to articulate a common process or ingredient owns it in the prospect's mind — Schlitz claimed 'every bottle washed with live steam' first and owned 'purity'.
competitor-positioning.best_query: preemptive claim Hopkins Schlitz live steam own common claim first to say

competitor-positioning.name: USP Pre-emption & The Deceptive Differential Test
competitor-positioning.source: Rosser Reeves, Reality in Advertising
competitor-positioning.one_line: Once a USP is established via penetration, a competitor copying it only advertises the leader; the moat is penetration not truth. The Deceptive Differential Test checks whether the claimed difference is actually perceivable after purchase.
competitor-positioning.use_in_skill: 03 (competitor analysis), 04 (offer — validating a claim is defensible and real)
competitor-positioning.best_query: USP preemption penetration moat deceptive differential test observable difference

competitor-positioning.name: The Advertising Burning Glass / Rule of One
competitor-positioning.source: Rosser Reeves, Reality in Advertising (Ch. 9); Hopkins; Sugarman
competitor-positioning.one_line: An ad must focus all selling power into one dominant concept like a burning glass focuses sunlight; the consumer remembers one thing. One reader, one big idea, one promise, one offer.
competitor-positioning.best_query: advertising burning glass rule of one dominant concept one reader one promise

competitor-positioning.name: Vampire Claims / Vampire Video & Mosaic Structure of Claims
competitor-positioning.source: Rosser Reeves, Reality in Advertising
competitor-positioning.one_line: You can have many claims in one ad only if each is a structural pillar of the single USP ('columns supporting a dome'); vampire claims/video are secondary elements that attract attention to themselves and silently destroy selling power.
competitor-positioning.use_in_skill: 06 (copy — audit claim drift), 08 (creatives — visuals serve message), 09 (consistency audit)
competitor-positioning.best_query: vampire claims vampire video mosaic structure architectural support single USP

competitor-positioning.name: Penetration / Usage Pull Framework
competitor-positioning.source: Rosser Reeves, Reality in Advertising
competitor-positioning.one_line: Penetration = % who remember your claim; Usage Pull = % of aware people who become customers beyond baseline. The gap is advertising's measurable sales effect; penetration is volatile (half forget in 6 months).
competitor-positioning.best_query: penetration usage pull framework Reeves measurement advertising effect

competitor-positioning.name: The Multi-Million Dollar Error (don't change a winning campaign)
competitor-positioning.source: Rosser Reeves, Reality in Advertising
competitor-positioning.one_line: Changing an effective campaign restarts penetration from zero — the costliest mistake. Law of Calculated Risk: a strong-USP campaign has ~90% chance of success vs ~30% for image/mood advertising.
competitor-positioning.best_query: multi-million dollar error changing effective campaign restart penetration law of calculated risk

competitor-positioning.name: Principle of Dispersion (Reach Before Frequency)
competitor-positioning.source: Rosser Reeves, Reality in Advertising
competitor-positioning.one_line: Reaching more people once beats reaching fewer many times — first exposure has highest marginal impact, subsequent exposures diminish rapidly; prioritize new reach over saturating existing audiences.
competitor-positioning.best_query: Reeves principle of dispersion reach before frequency diminishing returns exposure

competitor-positioning.name: Ries & Trout Positioning — The Mental/Product Ladder
competitor-positioning.source: Al Ries & Jack Trout, Positioning: The Battle for Your Mind (1981)
competitor-positioning.one_line: The mind organizes brands on a ladder (one per category), rejects info that contradicts what's there, holds room for ~3 brands; positioning is what you do to the prospect's mind, not the product. Perception is reality.
competitor-positioning.use_in_skill: 03 (competitor analysis — map the ladder), 04 (offer/positioning), 07a (page planning positioning)
competitor-positioning.best_query: positioning Ries Trout mental ladder product ladder battle for the mind perception

competitor-positioning.name: Law of Leadership (Be First) & Amelia Earhart Strategy
competitor-positioning.source: Al Ries & Jack Trout, Positioning
competitor-positioning.one_line: The first brand into a position gets ~2x the share of No.2 and 4x No.3; if you can't be first in an existing category, create a new one you can be first in (Amelia Earhart, first WOMAN to fly the Atlantic).
competitor-positioning.use_in_skill: 04 (offer — category creation), 03 (competitor analysis), 01 (product research — ownable niches)
competitor-positioning.best_query: law of leadership be first category creation Amelia Earhart strategy first in mind

competitor-positioning.name: Cherchez le Creneau — 8 Types of Holes in the Mind
competitor-positioning.source: Al Ries & Jack Trout, Positioning
competitor-positioning.one_line: When leadership is taken, find an unoccupied mental space: size, high-price, low-price, sex/gender, age, time-of-day, distribution, heavy-user. Beware the Factory Creneau Trap and Technology Trap (a hole with no mental creneau).
competitor-positioning.best_query: cherchez le creneau eight types holes in the mind size price age gender distribution

competitor-positioning.name: The Against Position / Uncola & Repositioning the Competition
competitor-positioning.source: Al Ries & Jack Trout, Positioning
competitor-positioning.one_line: Position explicitly against the leader (Avis 'We try harder'; 7-Up 'the Uncola') or change the prospect's perception of the competitor to open a hole (Tylenol repositioned aspirin as stomach-irritating).
competitor-positioning.best_query: against position uncola repositioning the competition Avis Tylenol aspirin inconvenient truth

competitor-positioning.name: Positioning by Attribute / by User
competitor-positioning.source: Al Ries & Jack Trout, Positioning (applied to ecom)
competitor-positioning.one_line: Leader owns the obvious attribute (anti-aging); you choose a different defensible attribute (hydration) or position by who uses it (Marlboro cowboys, protein for women over 40) to create a new ladder where you're No.1.
competitor-positioning.best_query: positioning by attribute positioning by user different attribute new ladder ecom

competitor-positioning.name: F.W.M.T.S. (Forgot What Made Them Successful) / Line Extension Trap
competitor-positioning.source: Al Ries & Jack Trout, Positioning
competitor-positioning.one_line: Brands lose great positions by abandoning what worked, advertising aspirations instead of reinforcing (Avis dropping 'We try harder'); positioning is cumulative — keep the strategic position, refresh only the creative.
competitor-positioning.best_query: FWMTS forgot what made them successful line extension trap positioning cumulative consistency

competitor-positioning.name: Schwartz Market Sophistication — 5 Stages
competitor-positioning.source: Eugene Schwartz, Breakthrough Advertising (Ch. 3)
competitor-positioning.one_line: Markets pass through 5 stages by exposure to claims: (1) name the claim, (2) enlarge it, (3) new mechanism, (4) better/elaborated mechanism, (5) identity/connection. Each stage demands a different headline strategy.
competitor-positioning.best_query: market sophistication five stages Schwartz enlarge claim new mechanism identity skepticism

competitor-positioning.name: Schwartz Mechanization Stages — Name / Describe / Feature
competitor-positioning.source: Eugene Schwartz, Breakthrough Advertising (Ch. 11)
competitor-positioning.one_line: Three stages of mechanism proof tied to sophistication: Stage 1 name the mechanism, Stage 2 describe it (Promise-Reason Why, emotion not scientific discourse), Stage 3 feature it in the headline as a NEW WAY to get the old result.
competitor-positioning.best_query: Schwartz mechanization stages name describe feature mechanism promise reason why headline

competitor-positioning.name: New Mechanism / New Information / New Identity (The Big 3)
competitor-positioning.source: Eugene Schwartz, Breakthrough Advertising (course application)
competitor-positioning.one_line: In sophisticated markets (stages 3-5) simple claims fail; break resistance with a New Mechanism (new HOW/hope), New Information (reframe the problem / why past solutions failed), or New Identity (what using the product says about you).
competitor-positioning.best_query: new mechanism new information new identity Big 3 sophisticated market break resistance

competitor-positioning.name: Competitor Research Process (Extracting Claims)
competitor-positioning.source: Direct response course methodology (Hopkins/Reeves applied)
competitor-positioning.one_line: Define research parameters (product, geography, competitor type), identify key competitors, analyze messaging/hooks/big ideas, evaluate customer feedback to find differentiation opportunities, compiled into a research doc for copy.
competitor-positioning.best_query: competitor research process extracting claims messaging hooks customer feedback differentiation

competitor-positioning.name: Reconnaissance Engine (Competitive Research via Social)
competitor-positioning.source: Metodologia interna de copy (P2, v2)
competitor-positioning.one_line: Always-on competitive intel: become competitors' ideal customer (follow 3+ on IG/TikTok/YouTube, engage, join email lists) so the algorithm serves market content; screenshot, download and transcribe competitor videos (SnapInsta + Descript).
competitor-positioning.best_query: reconnaissance engine competitive research via social Instagram transcribe competitor videos algorithm

competitor-positioning.source: Fonte primária 2026 (P1) + metodologia interna de copy (P2, v2) + programa interno BR (P3) + metodologia interna de Meta Ads (P3) + livros
competitor-positioning.one_line: Mine customer language/fears/desires from competitor reviews, Amazon, Reddit (10+ comment threads), TikTok honest-reviews, ad comments, Q&A; 3+ sources per category produces far more accurate customer profiles for copy.
competitor-positioning.best_query: consumer insights database review mining Reddit Amazon ad comments three source lift customer language

competitor-positioning.name: Cloaker Breaking / Competitive Espionage
competitor-positioning.source: Direct response course methodology (advanced competitive intel)
competitor-positioning.one_line: Techniques to access competitor funnels hidden by cloakers; the goal is not to clone offers but to understand what is actually scaling behind the curtain to make better briefing decisions.
competitor-positioning.best_query: cloaker breaking competitive espionage hidden funnels what is scaling access competitor offer

competitor-positioning.name: Test-Then-Scale Method (applied to competitor claims)
competitor-positioning.source: Claude Hopkins, Scientific Advertising / My Life in Advertising
competitor-positioning.one_line: When you discover a competitor claim or angle, run a small keyed test in a limited market and only scale if the numbers prove it works for your product (Liquozone, Palmolive, Pepsodent city-tests).
competitor-positioning.best_query: Hopkins test then scale keyed coupon small city test before national competitor claim

competitor-positioning.name: Category Economics / 'Pork and Beans' Insight
competitor-positioning.source: Claude Hopkins, Scientific Advertising
competitor-positioning.one_line: Understanding the true competitive landscape — what behavior or habit you are actually replacing — matters more than understanding direct competitors (you compete against the status quo, not just rival brands).
competitor-positioning.best_query: Hopkins pork and beans category economics what behavior replacing true competition status quo

competitor-positioning.name: Swipe File Method & Handcopy Practice
competitor-positioning.source: Dan Kennedy, The Ultimate Sales Letter; Gary Halbert, The Boron Letters; Sugarman; Bly
competitor-positioning.one_line: Build a curated, categorized collection of proven ads (validated by longevity or shares) and internalize via handcopying winners and reading aloud; organize by headline/lead/guarantee/CTA/proof/offer/format and pattern from structure, not words.
competitor-positioning.best_query: swipe file method handcopy practice Kennedy collect organize winning ads patterning technique

competitor-positioning.name: Winning Ad Extraction / Processing Learnings
competitor-positioning.source: Direct response course methodology (AdSpy-validated study)
competitor-positioning.one_line: Validate winners via shares/engagement (AdSpy beats 'active' status), study the hook (why it stops scroll) and the whole (how it closes), asking 'why does this matter?' repeatedly to extract transferable STRATEGIES (not templates) even cross-niche.
competitor-positioning.best_query: winning ads extracting strategies process learnings AdSpy shares validated hook why it works

competitor-positioning.name: Kennedy USP Construction Formula
competitor-positioning.source: Dan Kennedy, Magnetic Marketing / No BS Direct Marketing
competitor-positioning.one_line: USP = Narrow Positioning + Meaningful Specifics + Guarantee. Choose one dimension to own (Domino's: speed + temperature, ignoring taste) — 'when you try to be everything to everyone you are nothing to everyone.'
competitor-positioning.best_query: Kennedy USP construction formula narrow positioning meaningful specifics guarantee Domino's

competitor-positioning.name: Ogilvy 'Positively Good' Strategy for Parity Products
competitor-positioning.source: David Ogilvy, Confessions of an Advertising Man
competitor-positioning.one_line: When your product performs identically to competitors, don't claim superiority — describe it as 'positively good' with such conviction and sensory specificity that readers assume it must be superior, because competitors rarely describe their own product that way.
competitor-positioning.best_query: Ogilvy positively good parity product strategy describe with conviction sensory detail

competitor-positioning.name: Ogilvy Brand Image Theory + Bird's Positioning Synthesis
competitor-positioning.source: David Ogilvy, Confessions; Drayton Bird, Commonsense Direct & Digital Marketing
competitor-positioning.one_line: Every ad is a long-term investment in the brand's total personality; Bird synthesizes positioning as Brand Image + USP — what the brand promises (USP) AND what it means (image) in the prospect's mind.
competitor-positioning.best_query: Ogilvy brand image theory Drayton Bird positioning brand image plus USP total personality

competitor-positioning.name: Inoculation Theory (pre-empt competitor attacks)
competitor-positioning.source: William McGuire (social psychology), applied in persuasion frameworks
competitor-positioning.one_line: Strengthen loyalty by presenting a WEAKENED version of a competitor's future argument and encouraging the prospect to mount their own defense — like a vaccine, a weak attack builds lasting resistance.
competitor-positioning.best_query: inoculation theory McGuire weakened competitor argument build resistance pre-empt loyalty

competitor-positioning.name: Storytelling as Hardest-to-Replicate Angle (Founder Story / Villain)
competitor-positioning.source: Fraser (Fraggle), Creative Strategy 102
competitor-positioning.one_line: Competitors can copy product, price and ad format but not your story; founder stories and villain-based narratives (positioning against the status quo / 'Big Shave' / subscriptions) are the most defensible differentiation.
competitor-positioning.best_query: storytelling hardest to replicate founder story villain narrative defensible angle status quo

competitor-positioning.name: Auditoria de Markup de Promos (método Kyle Milligan)
competitor-positioning.source: Kyle Milligan
competitor-positioning.one_line: Marca a promo do concorrente com um código de cores por tipo de bloco — objeção, claim, prova, benefício — transformando a leitura da peça em um inventário da estrutura que ela usa.
competitor-positioning.best_query: auditoria markup promo codigo de cores lexico de blocos objection claim proof benefit

competitor-positioning.name: As três práticas de estudo de swipe file (Markup Audit → Handcopy → Patterning)
competitor-positioning.source: Aura KB — tema 'Pesquisa de Mercado e Concorrencia' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
competitor-positioning.one_line: Três práticas de estudo de swipe file em ordem definida: primeiro auditar a peça com markup, depois copiá-la à mão e por fim extrair os padrões que se repetem entre peças.

competitor-positioning.name: Discovery por longevidade no Atria + validação por shares
competitor-positioning.source: Aura KB — tema 'Pesquisa de Mercado e Concorrencia' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)

competitor-positioning.name: Medição de escala do criativo na Ad Library (aparições = ad sets)
competitor-positioning.source: Aura KB — tema 'Pesquisa de Mercado e Concorrencia' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)

competitor-positioning.name: Ideation / Iteration / Imitation (3 modos de research)
competitor-positioning.source: Aura KB — tema 'Pesquisa de Mercado e Concorrencia' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)

competitor-positioning.name: Whitelisted/Affiliate Ad Discovery (buscar os termos, não a página)
competitor-positioning.source: Aura KB — tema 'Pesquisa de Mercado e Concorrencia' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)

competitor-positioning.name: 5 Positioning Strategies a partir dos gaps do concorrente
competitor-positioning.source: Aura KB — tema 'Pesquisa de Mercado e Concorrencia' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)

scaling.name: Profitable Scaling Margin (PSM)
scaling.source: Fonte primária 2026 (P1) / fonte primária high-ticket 2026 (P1) — fonte primária DTC/ecommerce, inclusive Meta Ads (hierarquia revisada 2026-09-01); metodologia interna de Meta Ads (P3) registrada como visão alternativa nomeada

scaling.source: Rosser Reeves (Reality in Advertising)

scaling.name: Spend Redistribution Framework (Don't Kill the Top Spender)
scaling.source: Fonte primária 2026 (P1) / fonte primária high-ticket 2026 (P1) — fonte primária DTC/ecommerce, inclusive Meta Ads (hierarquia revisada 2026-09-01); metodologia interna de Meta Ads (P3) registrada como visão alternativa nomeada

retention-email.name: Drayton Bird's Email = Direct Mail Principle
retention-email.source: Drayton Bird, Commonsense Direct and Digital Marketing
retention-email.one_line: Email obeys the same rules as direct mail: long copy can beat short, emails should come from a real person (not a brand), subject lines are headlines — medium changed, psychology didn't.
retention-email.best_query: Drayton Bird email direct mail principle long copy real person subject line headline

retention-email.name: The Rule of 1 (one goal / one job per element / one reader)
retention-email.source: Joanna Wiebe (Copyhackers)
retention-email.one_line: Every email has exactly 1 goal, every element has 1 job, and it's written to 1 person; start by writing the CTA that connects to the single goal.
retention-email.best_query: Rule of 1 email one goal one job per element one reader write CTA first

retention-email.name: 3-to-1 Value-to-Sales Rule
retention-email.source: Joanna Wiebe (Copyhackers)
retention-email.one_line: For every 3 value-creating emails you send, allow yourself 1 sales email — balances free/paid content and tips the scale toward goodwill.
retention-email.best_query: 3 to 1 rule value emails sales email balance newsletter cadence

retention-email.name: Fibonacci Drip-Cadence Sequence
retention-email.source: Joanna Wiebe (Copyhackers)
retention-email.one_line: Space drip emails on the Fibonacci sequence (Day 0,1,1,2,3,5,8,13...) — frequent early to train opens, then tapering so you keep ties without overwhelming.
retention-email.best_query: Fibonacci sequence drip campaign email cadence day 0 1 2 3 5 8 spacing Copyhackers

retention-email.name: Day Zero Triggered-Email Method (behavior-triggered mini-funnels)
retention-email.source: Joanna Wiebe / Copyhackers (programa interno de conversion copy, P3)
retention-email.one_line: Replace long time-based drips with many behavior-triggered 'Day Zero' standalone emails (Day 0 outperforms because it's tied to a just-taken action), each spun into a mini-funnel with a few time-triggered follow-ups capped ~Day 4.
retention-email.use_in_skill: 13 (architecture of triggered flows vs legacy drip)
retention-email.best_query: Day Zero behavior-triggered email mini-funnel outperforms time-based drip cap day 4

retention-email.name: 5-Step Welcome Sequence Process (welcome = lead-nurturing, not 'welcome')
retention-email.source: Joanna Wiebe / Copyhackers (welcome-sequence framework)
retention-email.one_line: Welcome sequences are lead-nurturing sequences that support sales (direct or indirect); built via a 5-step framework: VOC research → analyze → plan strategic sequence → write → automate/test — a framework, not a template.
retention-email.best_query: welcome sequence lead nurturing 5 step process VOC research plan automate not a template

retention-email.name: From-Name as Inbox Filter
retention-email.source: Joanna Wiebe (Copyhackers)
retention-email.one_line: On mobile Gmail the From name is the largest, top element — it's the real gatekeeper; use a recognizable real person, no symbols, not too formal, and test combos (e.g. 'Joanna, HubSpot'); different email types need different From names.
retention-email.best_query: From name inbox filter mobile Gmail gatekeeper real person test from line deliverability

retention-email.name: Engagement Suppression / Sunset & Double-Opt-In Re-engagement
retention-email.source: Joanna Wiebe / Copyhackers (list-hygiene automation pattern)
retention-email.one_line: Auto-suppress/unsubscribe non-engagers (e.g. wait 7 days for confirmation click, else remove) and run a separate re-engagement sequence before culling — protects deliverability and respects 30-day-engagement laws.
retention-email.use_in_skill: 13 (list hygiene / sunset flow protecting sender reputation)
retention-email.best_query: engagement suppression sunset re-engagement double opt-in unsubscribe non-engaged deliverability 30 day

retention-email.name: 30-60-90 Day LTV Email+SMS Flow Hacks (3-layer system)
retention-email.source: Aura methodology (retention/email-SMS-flows) [segundo nível na hierarquia revisada 2026-09-01: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna]
retention-email.one_line: Three layers — LTV as the goal, email+SMS as the weapons (email = conversation, SMS = nudge), zero-party data as the irreplaceable fuel — architected around the second-purchase window across day buckets 1-7 / 7-14 / 14-30 / 30-60 / 60-90.
retention-email.best_query: 30-60-90 day LTV email SMS flow hacks second purchase window zero-party data force multiplier

retention-email.name: Zero-Party Data Moat
retention-email.source: Aura methodology (retention) [segundo nível na hierarquia revisada 2026-09-01: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna]
retention-email.one_line: Voluntarily-shared customer data (post-purchase surveys, onboarding quizzes, preference centers, checkout questions) personalizes flows competitors literally cannot replicate — the moat is the data, not the tech.
retention-email.use_in_skill: 13 (personalization layer of retention flows) and 04 (offer/data capture design)
retention-email.best_query: zero-party data moat post-purchase survey onboarding quiz preference center unreplicable personalization

retention-email.name: Email/SMS Coordination Rule (echo, don't collide)
retention-email.source: Aura methodology (retention/SMS) [segundo nível na hierarquia revisada 2026-09-01: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna]
retention-email.one_line: Never send email and SMS simultaneously about the same thing — send email first with the full story, follow 4-24h later with SMS to non-openers; SMS for time-sensitive actions, email for education/story.
retention-email.best_query: email SMS coordination echo not collide send email first SMS follow up non-openers staggered cadence

retention-email.name: Abandoned-Cart Decay Curve + Two Sequence Styles (Discount vs Emotion)
retention-email.source: Aura methodology (built on Baymard Institute data + classic frameworks) [segundo nível na hierarquia revisada 2026-09-01: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna]
retention-email.one_line: Recovery is time-critical (steep decay, ~69.8% Baymard abandon rate); two playbooks — Discount-focused (escalating 20-30%+ discount Day0→final) vs Emotion-focused (delay discount to Day 3); hit hard early (Day 0 + 6h), taper, escalate near the cliff.
retention-email.best_query: abandoned cart decay curve Baymard 69.8% discount-focused emotion-focused sequence escalating discount day 0 6 hours

retention-email.name: 5 Reasons People Abandon (objection map)
retention-email.source: Aura methodology (abandon-cart psychology) [segundo nível na hierarquia revisada 2026-09-01: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna]
retention-email.one_line: Abandonment (and non-purchase generally) traces to 5 causes — price/cost, lack of urgency (air-conditioner effect), negative past experiences, incomplete information, lack of trust/skepticism — each maps to an email in the sequence (e.g. Day 2 FAQ resolves incomplete info).
retention-email.best_query: five reasons people abandon cart price urgency negative experience incomplete information skepticism objection map

retention-email.name: Restock / Testimonial / Anniversary Coupon Welcome-Series Beats
retention-email.source: Aura methodology (ecommerce welcome/retention) [segundo nível na hierarquia revisada 2026-09-01: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna]
retention-email.one_line: Post-purchase ecommerce welcome series moves to weekly after heavy early sends, layering recurring beats: restock coupon, testimonial request (~week 5), 'missed promo' apology coupon, anniversary/keep-using reminder coupon (~week 8).
retention-email.best_query: ecommerce welcome series restock coupon testimonial week 5 anniversary coupon weekly post-purchase beats

retention-email.name: Seasonal Abandoned-Cart SMS Update Checklist
retention-email.source: Aura methodology (SMS/seasonal) [segundo nível na hierarquia revisada 2026-09-01: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna]
retention-email.one_line: To convert an evergreen abandoned-cart SMS for a seasonal sale: 1) swap in optimized seasonal offer details, 2) add campaign details (sale name + exact close time), 3) layer urgency (loss aversion, 'no rain check'), 4) layer real scarcity only if it exists.
retention-email.use_in_skill: 13 (seasonal SMS) and overlaps with seasonal/BFCM campaign work
retention-email.best_query: seasonal abandoned cart SMS update checklist offer details campaign close time urgency scarcity no rain check

retention-email.name: Versão Sem Headline para Lista Quente (a frente como módulo destacável)
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Direct Response Foundations (Principios Classicos)' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Duas versões da mesma carta: uma com o bloco de headline na frente e outra abrindo direto no "Dear Reader", tratando a abertura como módulo destacável para quando a lista já está aquecida.
retention-email.best_query: mesma carta com bloco de headline e abrindo direto em Dear Reader lista aquecida

retention-email.name: Self-Segmenter Email (explicit ask vs subtle ask)
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Copywriting para Emails' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Email que pede ao assinante para se classificar sozinho, na forma explícita ou na sutil, com links que aplicam tag por segmento e no máximo 5 opções; entra como segundo email do day zero.
retention-email.best_query: self-segmenter email links com tag por segmento maximo 5 opcoes segundo email do day zero

retention-email.name: Conditional Messaging (um email, vários segmentos)
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Copywriting para Emails' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Monta um único email capaz de atender sete segmentos por meio de blocos condicionais, partindo do custo invisível que um email irrelevante cobra da lista.
retention-email.best_query: conditional messaging um email para sete segmentos custo invisivel de email irrelevante

retention-email.name: Arquitetura Confirmation → Self-Segmenter → Welcome
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Copywriting para Emails' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Sequência de entrada em três etapas: confirmação do lead magnet com double opt-in por clique, email de auto-segmentação e só então a welcome, separando lista de freebie de lista de newsletter.
retention-email.best_query: sequencia de confirmacao por lead magnet double opt-in por clique lista freebie vs newsletter

retention-email.name: Hot-Time Anchor
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Copywriting para Emails' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Regra de disparo que segura o envio até as 6am ou as 5pm no fuso do próprio contato, montando a condição com OR e nunca com AND.
retention-email.best_query: hot time anchor esperar ate 6am ou 5pm no fuso do contato usar OR nunca AND

retention-email.name: Profit-Propellant SMS Equation
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Copywriting para SMS' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Equação que reduz a mensagem de SMS ao seu device persuasivo e vai somando elementos de oferta em cima dele, em vez de escrever texto solto.
retention-email.best_query: profit propellant SMS equation reduzir mensagem ao device persuasivo somar elementos de oferta

retention-email.name: Métricas de SMS (EPM / CTR / UNSUB) + benchmarks
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Copywriting para SMS' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Painel de métricas de SMS montado em torno de EPM (earning per message), CTR e unsub, com benchmarks de 8,11 para abandoned cart e 1,04 para campanha.
retention-email.best_query: EPM earning per message CTR unsub benchmark abandoned cart 8,11 campanha 1,04

retention-email.name: Seis Estratégias de Segmentação de SMS
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Copywriting para SMS' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Seis cortes de segmentação aplicáveis a SMS: clientes novos versus recorrentes, tempo desde a última compra, VIPs, por produto e por localização.
retention-email.best_query: seis segmentacoes SMS novos versus recorrentes ultima compra VIP por produto por localizacao

retention-email.name: MMS Copy Overlay + regra de janela
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Copywriting para SMS' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Uso de MMS com copy sobreposta à imagem para engajar pelo lado emocional, mais a regra de janela que evita MMS nas últimas horas da promoção.
retention-email.best_query: MMS copy overlay imagem que engaja o coracao evitar MMS nas ultimas horas da promo

retention-email.name: Thank-You Page Surveys (2 perguntas, rodadas em sequência)
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Copywriting para Web Pages' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Pesquisa de duas perguntas na thank-you page, rodadas uma de cada vez em sequência, abrindo com "o que estava acontecendo na sua vida que te trouxe até aqui".
retention-email.best_query: thank you page survey o que estava acontecendo na sua vida que te trouxe ate aqui

retention-email.name: A-Pile vs B-Pile (teoria do envelope aplicada a subject line/hero)
retention-email.source: Dan Kennedy, The Ultimate Sales Letter / No BS Direct Marketing
retention-email.one_line: Transporta a teoria do envelope — a pilha que se abre e a que se descarta — para a subject line e o hero, usando sinais como parecer pessoal e urgente, o selo real e a ausência de marca.
retention-email.best_query: A-pile B-pile envelope parece pessoal e urgente selo real ausencia de marca

retention-email.name: Take Rate Primeiro + churn spike de ~dia 45
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Retencao e Email Marketing' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Otimizar primeiro o take rate da assinatura e só depois o churn, sabendo que o pico de cancelamento cai por volta do dia 45; o subscribe and save entra pelo back-end antes de virar oferta de entrada.
retention-email.best_query: take rate antes de churn, pico de cancelamento no dia 45, subscribe and save no back-end primeiro

retention-email.name: Save-a-Churn Calls + o truque de packaging
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Retencao e Email Marketing' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Um VA liga para quem pediu cancelamento e salva o cliente ao custo de 9 dólares de COGS; junto vem o truque de embalagem, em que reduzir o pacote antecipa a recompra.
retention-email.best_query: VA liga para quem vai cancelar, salvar cliente por 9 dólares de COGS, reduzir embalagem antecipa a recompra

retention-email.name: Sequência de Abandoned Cart com voz de persona (Haddad)
retention-email.source: Haddad (long-form direct-response practitioner)
retention-email.one_line: Sequência de carrinho abandonado escrita na voz de uma persona, com o girlfriend deal, a linha "se você já comprou, ignore esta mensagem" e um testemunho do marido no P.S.
retention-email.best_query: girlfriend deal, se você já comprou ignore esta mensagem, testemunho do marido no P.S.

retention-email.name: Daily Email System / Infotainment (Ben Settle) — o esqueleto do broadcast
retention-email.source: Ben Settle
retention-email.one_line: Esqueleto do broadcast diário de infotainment: abertura punchy, história, a virada do "the point?", lição em três linhas e o mesmo link todo dia.
retention-email.best_query: abertura punchy, story, the point?, lição em 3 linhas, mesmo link todo dia

retention-email.name: Motor de Suprimento Diário de Ideias (4 fontes de pauta)
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Retencao e Email Marketing' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Quatro fontes de pauta que resolvem o "o que dizer amanhã" do email diário, entre elas o que o mercado está reclamando e as reviews negativas de livros do nicho.
retention-email.best_query: o que dizer amanhã, o que o mercado está reclamando, reviews negativas de livros do nicho

retention-email.name: Os 10 Arquétipos de Email de Campanha (Settle)
retention-email.source: Ben Settle
retention-email.one_line: Dez formatos recorrentes de email de campanha — contrarian take, quote opener de série, testimonial story, Q&A de assinante, resposta a troll — para variar o broadcast sem partir do zero.
retention-email.best_query: contrarian take, quote opener de série, testimonial story, Q&A de assinante, resposta a troll

retention-email.name: Soft Information vs Hard Information (diga O QUE, nunca COMO)
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Retencao e Email Marketing' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Separa dizer O QUE fazer de dizer COMO fazer: o email entrega apenas o quê, mantém a cenoura pendurada e reserva o how para dentro do produto.
retention-email.best_query: dizer o que fazer sem dizer como fazer, dangling the carrot, o how é o produto

retention-email.name: Taxonomia de Subject Lines de Ben Settle (5 categorias, arquivo de 2.684 emails)
retention-email.source: Ben Settle
retention-email.one_line: Cinco categorias de subject line extraídas de um arquivo de 2.684 emails: chocante, bizarro, curiosidade, inversão de ditados populares e reaproveitamento de vencedoras.
retention-email.best_query: shocking bizarre curiosity flipping popular sayings reused winners

retention-email.name: Formato Editor-Endorsement para lista fria/afiliado (Haddad)
retention-email.source: Haddad (long-form direct-response practitioner)
retention-email.one_line: Formato em que o email não vem do dono da oferta e sim de um editor de publicação que a endossa, com três links âncora apontando para o mesmo destino; feito para lista fria e tráfego de afiliado.
retention-email.best_query: email não vem do dono da oferta, editor de publicação endossa, 3 links âncora para o mesmo destino

retention-email.name: In Media Res + o hook "I never thought it was possible, but ___"
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Retencao e Email Marketing' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Abrir cortando as cinco primeiras linhas e jogando o leitor no meio da batalha, pulando tudo o que ele já pularia, com o hook "I never thought it was possible, but ___".
retention-email.best_query: corte as 5 primeiras linhas, jogue o leitor no meio da batalha, skip everything the reader skips

retention-email.name: Três caminhos de segmentação + Segmentation Worksheet (segmento pelo produto a vender)
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Retencao e Email Marketing' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)

retention-email.name: Playbook Q4 de Email & SMS (targeting pyramid + "texting without selling")
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Retencao e Email Marketing' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Playbook de Q4 que trata email como canal de volume e SMS como canal cirúrgico, com pirâmide de targeting por engajamento (30, 90 e dormentes de 120 dias), quiet hours do Texas e a prática de texting without selling.
retention-email.best_query: email tolera volume SMS é cirúrgico, engaged 30 engaged 90 dormant 120, quiet hours texas

retention-email.name: Campanha de 4 Dias e os 6 templates
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Retencao e Email Marketing' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Campanha sazonal de quatro dias montada com seis templates prontos, incluindo o template da inveja e o tratamento do dia de slump no meio da promoção.
retention-email.best_query: campanha sazonal de 4 dias com 6 templates, dia de slump, template da inveja

retention-email.name: Four-Part Sales Drip (Possible Impossible / Special Case / Five Inches Five Miles / Ice Water)
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Retencao e Email Marketing' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Drip de venda em quatro emails: o primeiro iguala o ceticismo e sobe com um caso incrível, o seguinte trata o "isso não vai funcionar pra mim", e os demais cruzam benefício imediato com benefício distante.

retention-email.name: As 5 sub-sequências de Ry Schwartz (Segmentação → Pré-Launch → Launch → Sales → Closing)
retention-email.source: Eugene Schwartz, Breakthrough Advertising
retention-email.one_line: Cinco sub-sequências encadeadas de segmentação a fechamento, com hard sell na crença e soft sell no produto, o email "o que isso diz sobre você" e o anti-launch launch email.
retention-email.best_query: hard sell na crença e soft sell no produto, o que isso diz sobre você, anti-launch launch email

retention-email.name: As 5 Camadas de Crença (perguntas exploratórias de campanha)
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Retencao e Email Marketing' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Cinco camadas de crença mapeadas por perguntas exploratórias: o que o leitor precisa acreditar sobre o resultado, sobre as próprias falhas passadas e sobre as vacas sagradas do mercado.
retention-email.best_query: o que precisam acreditar sobre o resultado, sobre as falhas passadas, sobre as vacas sagradas do mercado

retention-email.name: Os 3 templates de maior alavancagem: "Here's What This Says About You", Upgraded FAQ Close e Perfect-For-You-If
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Retencao e Email Marketing' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Três templates de maior alavancagem: o email de confirmação que devolve ao leitor o significado do clique, o FAQ close turbinado com as perguntas feitas antes do sim, e o perfect-for-you-if em que se marca 4 das 6 caixas.

retention-email.name: Fórmula de Reorder + Winback com desconto progressivo
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Retencao e Email Marketing' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Recompra disparada 7 dias antes de o estoque do cliente acabar, com o arco "você está progredindo, vai progredir mais, continue ou vai perder o progresso", seguida de winback com desconto progressivo.
retention-email.best_query: você está progredindo vai progredir mais continue vai perder o progresso, 7 dias antes de acabar o estoque

retention-email.name: Referral Growth Equation + Goodwill = Value − Price + as 7 formas de pedir
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Retencao e Email Marketing' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Crescimento entendido como indicações que entram menos churn que sai, apoiado no goodwill acumulado antes do pedido (valor menos preço) e em sete formas de pedir a indicação, incluindo incentivo de dois lados.

retention-email.name: 5 perguntas de Miller para depoimentos de transformação + insight reclamação-lealdade de Bird
retention-email.source: Donald Miller
retention-email.one_line: Cinco perguntas que extraem depoimentos de transformação — qual era o problema antes, qual era a frustração, o que foi diferente, como foi a transformação — somadas ao insight sobre a relação entre reclamação e lealdade.
retention-email.best_query: qual era o problema antes, qual era a frustração, o que foi diferente, como foi a transformação

retention-email.name: Self-Segmenter Sequence (tag por goal antes da welcome)

retention-email.name: Sequências promocionais formulaicas (Holiday 3 / Black Friday 6 / Flash Sale 24h 3)
retention-email.source: Al Ries & Jack Trout, Positioning
retention-email.one_line: Três formatos fechados de promoção — 3 emails para datas comemorativas, 6 para Black Friday e 3 para flash sale de 24 horas — cada um com razão declarada para a sale e recomendação de estocar.
retention-email.best_query: razão para a sale, stock up recommendation, sale de 24 horas não planejada

retention-email.name: The You Rule + One Idea Per Sentence + fórmulas de CTA que sobem clique
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Retencao e Email Marketing' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Três regras de escrita: reescrever cada frase começando por "você", varrer os "e", "ou" e "mas" atrás de frases com duas ideias, e usar CTA em primeira pessoa no botão ("eu quero ___").
retention-email.best_query: reescreva toda frase começando com você, varrer and or but em busca de duas ideias, eu quero ___ no botão

retention-email.name: Email Diagnosis Checklist (uma métrica, um elemento, um trabalho)
retention-email.source: Aura KB — tema 'Retencao e Email Marketing' (segundo nível: livros / swipe files / masterclass interna)
retention-email.one_line: Checklist que liga cada métrica a um elemento e a um trabalho: open rate baixo aponta para from name e subject, click baixo para o match entre hook e corpo, e bounce para o message match com a H1 da página.

persuasion-psychology.name: Cialdini's Six Weapons of Influence
persuasion-psychology.source: Robert Cialdini — Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Six automatic 'click-whirr' compliance triggers: Reciprocation, Commitment/Consistency, Social Proof, Liking (5 factors), Authority (titles/clothes/trappings), Scarcity (loss aversion + reactance).
persuasion-psychology.use_in_skill: 06 (copy), 08 (creatives), 10 (ad strategy) — map each persuasion lever onto copy blocks and ad angles.
persuasion-psychology.best_query: Cialdini six weapons of influence reciprocity commitment social proof authority liking scarcity

persuasion-psychology.name: Cialdini's 13 Compliance Techniques
persuasion-psychology.source: Robert Cialdini — Influence
persuasion-psychology.one_line: 13 named tactics: rejection-then-retreat, foot-in-the-door, lowball, limited-number, deadline, benefactor-before-beggar, BUG device, good cop/bad cop, talking the top of the line, argue against own interest, etc.
persuasion-psychology.use_in_skill: 04 (offer), 06 (copy), 10 (ad strategy) — choose compliance mechanics for offer architecture and CTAs.
persuasion-psychology.best_query: Cialdini 13 compliance techniques rejection-then-retreat foot-in-the-door lowball deadline tactic

persuasion-psychology.name: The Unity Principle (7th Weapon)
persuasion-psychology.source: Robert Cialdini — Pre-Suasion / Influence (expanded edition)
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Shared identity ('one of us' not merely 'like us') via Being Together (kinship/family language, 97% compliance) and Acting Together (synchrony, asking advice not opinion).
persuasion-psychology.use_in_skill: 06 (copy), 13 (retention/community), 08 (UGC creatives) — brand-as-tribe framing and family language.
persuasion-psychology.best_query: Cialdini Unity principle seventh weapon being together acting together asking advice merger mindset

persuasion-psychology.name: Pre-Suasion Model (Attractors & Magnetizers)
persuasion-psychology.source: Robert Cialdini — Pre-Suasion
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Channel what is focal BEFORE the message: Attractors seize attention (sexual, threatening, novel); Magnetizers hold it (self-referential 'you', the Unfinished/Zeigarnik, the Mysterious). Focus = importance = causality.
persuasion-psychology.best_query: Pre-Suasion privileged moments attractors magnetizers Zeigarnik unfinished self-referential focus causality

persuasion-psychology.name: If/When-Then Plans
persuasion-psychology.source: Robert Cialdini — Pre-Suasion
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Implementation intentions that pre-load a behavioral trigger ('When X happens, then I will do Y'), dramatically lifting follow-through (e.g. appointment no-show reduction).
persuasion-psychology.best_query: If-When-Then plans implementation intentions Pre-Suasion Cialdini commitment activation

persuasion-psychology.name: Fluency Effect
persuasion-psychology.source: Robert Cialdini — Pre-Suasion (also Whitman/Cashvertising)
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Easy-to-process messages are automatically trusted, liked and valued more — easier names, readable fonts, rhymes all raise compliance. Clarity is a persuasion tool, not just readability.
persuasion-psychology.best_query: fluency effect cognitive ease rhyme as reason easy to process trust persuasion

persuasion-psychology.name: Reciprocity Optimization Triad
persuasion-psychology.source: Robert Cialdini — Pre-Suasion
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Reciprocity maximizes when the gift is Significant + Unexpected + Personalized (waiter-mints study, +23% tips). All three required.
persuasion-psychology.best_query: reciprocity optimization triad significant unexpected personalized gift waiter mints Pre-Suasion

persuasion-psychology.name: Contrast Principle
persuasion-psychology.source: Robert Cialdini — Influence
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Two items presented in sequence exaggerate their difference (show rundown house first, expensive suit before accessories) — amplifies every other weapon, esp. price anchoring.
persuasion-psychology.best_query: contrast principle Cialdini sequential presentation exaggerated difference price anchoring

persuasion-psychology.name: CLARCCS Framework
persuasion-psychology.source: Drew Eric Whitman — Cashvertising
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Ad-specific adaptation of Cialdini for the peripheral route, low-involvement buys: Comparison, Liking, Authority, Reciprocation, Commitment, Scarcity.
persuasion-psychology.use_in_skill: 08 (creatives), 10 (ad strategy) — quick checklist for ad-level persuasion cues.
persuasion-psychology.best_query: Cashvertising CLARCCS comparison liking authority reciprocation commitment scarcity Whitman

persuasion-psychology.name: Cashvertising Life-Force 8 (LF8)
persuasion-psychology.source: Drew Eric Whitman — Cashvertising
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Eight biologically hardwired desires driving more sales than all others combined (survival, food/drink, freedom from fear/pain, sex, comfort, superiority/winning, protection of loved ones, social approval).
persuasion-psychology.best_query: Cashvertising Life-Force 8 LF8 eight biological desires survival social approval superiority Whitman

persuasion-psychology.name: Cashvertising 9 Learned Wants + Desire Formula

persuasion-psychology.name: Four-Step Fear Appeal
persuasion-psychology.source: Pratkanis & Aronson — Age of Propaganda
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Fear appeals only work with all four: Scare (vivid threat) + Recommend (specific action) + Prove effectiveness + Prove accessibility (ordinary people can do it). Listerine/halitosis case.

persuasion-psychology.name: Inoculation Theory
persuasion-psychology.source: William McGuire (cited via Pratkanis & Aronson / Age of Propaganda)
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Pre-emptive defense: warn of competitor attack, present competitor argument in WEAKENED form, prompt prospect's own rebuttal — builds lasting resistance like a vaccine. Attack must be weak.
persuasion-psychology.best_query: inoculation theory McGuire weakened attack pre-emptive defense competitor argument resistance

persuasion-psychology.name: Elaboration Likelihood Model (Central vs Peripheral)
persuasion-psychology.source: Petty & Cacioppo (cited via Pratkanis & Aronson)
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Two routes to persuasion: Central (facts/evidence, durable attitude as 'brainchild', high-involvement) vs Peripheral (images/humor/celebrity, fast but fragile, low-involvement).
