persuasion-psychology.name: Length-Implies-Strength Heuristic
persuasion-psychology.source: Pratkanis & Aronson — Age of Propaganda
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Sheer volume of content is itself a persuasion cue ('22 reasons to buy', 101-testimonial brochures) — more material reads as more true.
persuasion-psychology.best_query: length implies strength heuristic volume of content persuasion cue numbered reasons testimonials

persuasion-psychology.name: Bandwagon Effect (3 Group Types)
persuasion-psychology.source: Drew Eric Whitman / Pratkanis & Aronson
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Conformity pressure via aspirational groups (want to join), associative groups (already belong), dissociative groups (want to avoid).
persuasion-psychology.best_query: bandwagon effect aspirational associative dissociative groups social pressure conformity

persuasion-psychology.name: Ego Morphing / Vanity Appeal
persuasion-psychology.source: Pratkanis & Aronson — Age of Propaganda
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Consumers attracted to products reflecting who they are/want to be; identification (men drawn to images of men, women of women) not attraction.
persuasion-psychology.best_query: ego morphing vanity appeal identification consumers products reflect identity who they want to be

persuasion-psychology.name: Decoy Effect (Asymmetric Dominance)
persuasion-psychology.source: Dan Ariely — Predictably Irrational (Huber & Puto; Simonson & Tversky)
persuasion-psychology.one_line: An inferior third option shifts choice toward the option that dominates it (Economist: print-only decoy drove combo from 32% to 84%). The option nobody buys can be most profitable.
persuasion-psychology.best_query: decoy effect asymmetric dominance Economist Ariely pricing tiers print-only combo

persuasion-psychology.name: Social Norms vs Market Norms
persuasion-psychology.source: Dan Ariely — Predictably Irrational (Clark & Mills)
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Social (warm/reciprocal) and market (transactional) norms are incompatible; introducing money into a social exchange destroys it near-irreversibly (Israeli daycare fine, AARP lawyers).

persuasion-psychology.name: Hot-Cold Empathy Gap
persuasion-psychology.source: Ariely & Loewenstein — Predictably Irrational
persuasion-psychology.one_line: People underestimate by 72-420% how differently they act in emotional 'hot' vs rational 'cold' states; sell during hot states (post-pain, live events, scarcity-triggered).

persuasion-psychology.name: Endowment Effect / Virtual Ownership
persuasion-psychology.source: Thaler; Kahneman/Knetsch/Thaler — via Ariely (Duke basketball ticket study)
persuasion-psychology.one_line: People value what they own ~2x more; create endowment pre-purchase via free trials, future-pacing, 'imagine yourself' copy, liberal returns.
persuasion-psychology.best_query: endowment effect virtual ownership Duke basketball tickets free trial future pacing imagine yourself

persuasion-psychology.name: Door-Closing Aversion
persuasion-psychology.source: Shin & Ariely (2004) — Predictably Irrational
persuasion-psychology.one_line: People irrationally resist losing options even when worthless; 'offer expires midnight', 'only 3 spots', disappearing bonuses all exploit fear of a door closing.
persuasion-psychology.best_query: door-closing aversion loss of options Shin Ariely expires midnight only 3 spots disappearing bonus

persuasion-psychology.name: Zero Price Effect (FREE)
persuasion-psychology.source: Shampanier, Mazar & Ariely — Predictably Irrational
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Dropping price to zero produces a qualitative jump in perceived value (Lindt vs Hershey's at 1c→FREE; Amazon France 1-franc vs free shipping). 'Free' ≠ 'almost free'.

persuasion-psychology.name: Precommitment Mechanisms
persuasion-psychology.source: Ariely (Predictably Irrational); Thaler & Sunstein
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Binding to a course before temptation improves follow-through; early opt-ins/deposits/calendared calls and prepaid annual plans reduce churn and raise purchase likelihood.

persuasion-psychology.name: Anchoring & Adjustment
persuasion-psychology.source: Tversky & Kahneman (1974) — via Priceless (Poundstone) & Ariely
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Estimates cling to an available number, even irrelevant ones (SSN auction, real-estate listing study); set a high anchor first and own the reference price.

persuasion-psychology.name: Coherent Arbitrariness
persuasion-psychology.source: Ariely, Loewenstein & Prelec (2003) — Predictably Irrational / Priceless
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Relative price ratios are stable but absolute levels are arbitrary, set by the first anchor (Starbucks broke the coffee anchor to charge 4x).

persuasion-psychology.name: Prospect Theory (Reference Dependence + Loss Aversion)

persuasion-psychology.one_line: Outcomes judged as gains/losses vs a reference point; losses hurt ~2x; fourfold risk pattern. Frame acceptance as gain, rejection as loss.

persuasion-psychology.name: Price-Expectation Effect (Price as Placebo)
persuasion-psychology.source: Dan Ariely — Predictably Irrational (SoBe / Veladone-Rx studies)
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Higher price raises expected AND actual experienced quality (placebo pill, SoBe anagram study) — discounting can reduce real product effectiveness.

persuasion-psychology.name: Extremeness Aversion + Three-Tier Pricing
persuasion-psychology.source: Simonson & Tversky (1992) — via Priceless (Poundstone)
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Buyers avoid cheapest and dearest, gravitate to the middle (beer experiment); always offer three tiers with the middle as target.

persuasion-psychology.name: Schwartz Gradualization / Believability Bridge

persuasion-psychology.source: Eugene Schwartz — Breakthrough Advertising (Ch. 2)

persuasion-psychology.source: Eugene Schwartz — Breakthrough Advertising (Ch. 11)

persuasion-psychology.name: Schwartz Redefinition / Identification (Roles)
persuasion-psychology.source: Eugene Schwartz — Breakthrough Advertising (Ch. 8 & 10)
persuasion-psychology.one_line: Redefinition: simplification, escalation, price-reduction reframes; Identification: character roles & achievement roles — sell WHO they want to be.

persuasion-psychology.source: Eugene Schwartz — Breakthrough Advertising

persuasion-psychology.name: Schwartz Deadly Sincerity & The Turn
persuasion-psychology.source: Eugene Schwartz — Breakthrough Advertising

persuasion-psychology.name: Blair Warren's One-Sentence Persuasion
persuasion-psychology.source: Blair Warren — The One Sentence Persuasion Course

persuasion-psychology.source: Ellen Langer (Xerox study) — via Bencivenga Bullets

persuasion-psychology.source: Gary Bencivenga — Bencivenga Bullets
